title: Native K-flat tensor identification for the condensed action site
statement: For $A,G$ and an action-site presentation $P$ [def-sfb-condensed-inflation-action-site-data], use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in the fixed coefficient universe. A pure total-tensor comparison is a family of isomorphisms from the image of the original action total tensor to the native ringed-site total tensor, equal on every generalized pure-tensor summand, in every integer bidegree, to the original section identification. A site tensor model for a strong monoidal core of the derived action-site equivalence consists of this comparison, preservation of K-flat complexes, and the commuting localization comparison square for every pair with first factor K-flat. The square uses the original derived action tensor [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup] and native representative maps of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, def-zl-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal-data]. Define native tensor identification to mean the existence of a closed tensor-Hom structure with its canonical K-flat models, native signed symmetry, associator and both unitors, and a strong monoidal core for the derived action-site equivalence satisfying this site tensor model, preserving that symmetry, and identifying the original regular coefficient unit with the actual localized ring unit. The native target structures are constrained by their independent representative models; no alternative transported tensor is substituted.
